prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S105: Morrowglass issues a Dispatch Wave Amendment when a destination, priority, or load sequence changes after wave preparation has begun.
S106: Outbound Dispatch Sorter receives the Dispatch Wave Amendment and applies its authorized changes to outbound staging.
S107: The sorter preserves committed pallet order unless the amendment explicitly authorizes a change.
S108: Autonomous Forklift Fleet is introduced under the alias Larkspur.
S109: The fleet accepts work only when its vehicle status, assigned operating area, and required travel path are valid.
S110: Each vehicle selects an available task according to dispatch priority, battery condition, and proximity to the pickup point.
S111: Route selection accounts for aisle access, transfer-point readiness, pedestrian controls, and temporary operating restrictions.
S112: Vehicles confirm pallet identity and pickup location before lifting a load.
S113: The fleet limits speed and turning rates to protect pallet stability and maintain safe clearance from warehouse structures.
S114: During outbound preparation, the fleet assembles the data needed to document each completed transfer and its receiving position.
S115: Autonomous Forklift Fleet produces the Forklift Handoff Confirmation after the transfer is complete.
S116: Handoff reporting records the vehicle identifier, pallet identifier, transfer time, and any incomplete or deferred movement.
S117: Fire Alarm Panel produces the Sprinkler Zone Inhibit Notice when the applicable fire-protection condition is detected.
S118: Vehicles stop or reroute when active safety controls prevent entry to an assigned travel area.
S119: East Transfer Conveyor and West Transfer Conveyor provide designated interfaces for moving pallets between vehicle travel and outbound staging.
S120: Pallet Dimension Scanner measurements support route and handling decisions for loads that exceed standard pallet envelopes.
S121: Outbound Dispatch Sorter verifies that staging positions match the current outbound plan before loading begins.
S122: Shipping Documentation Desk prepares shipment records from the confirmed pallet and destination data.
S123: Warehouse Operations Supervisor reviews delayed tasks, abnormal vehicle stops, and unresolved staging constraints before releasing the next outbound wave.
S124: Warehouse Management System maintains the authoritative task state for pallet movements, inventory status, and operating priorities.
S125: Coordination depends on timely status updates so each operating area can act on current work without duplicating assignments.
S126: Work requests should include a unique task reference, a destination, and any operating constraints needed for safe execution.
S127: Yard Gate Controller validates arriving vehicle information against the active receiving plan before directing a vehicle onward.
S128: Yard Gate Controller records unresolved discrepancies for review and prevents an affected vehicle from proceeding when the discrepancy creates an operating risk.
S129: Yard Gate Controller uses the exception note to manage a receiving discrepancy at the gate.
S130: The receiving exception remains visible to the Warehouse Operations Supervisor until the discrepancy has been assessed and resolved.
S131: Inbound Inspection Desk records inspection outcomes before pallets enter routine warehouse handling.
S132: Inbound Pallet Buffer provides a controlled staging point when inspection or downstream handling is not yet ready.
S133: Pallet Dimension Scanner supplies measurements used to identify pallets that require a different handling path.
S134: Conveyor Line Controller coordinates conveyor movement and stops affected equipment when a downstream condition prevents safe transfer.
S135: East Transfer Conveyor and West Transfer Conveyor provide separate routes for moving pallets between operating areas.
S136: Autonomous Forklift Fleet receives work only when a route and destination are available for the assigned vehicle.
S137: North Aisle Stacker Crane and South Aisle Stacker Crane report operating availability so task allocation can account for equipment status.
S138: The Warehouse Operations Supervisor can defer work when a route conflict, equipment fault, or staging constraint remains unresolved.
S139: Maintenance Release Terminal is also known as Copperfield.
S140: Maintenance Release Terminal produces the Crane Service Release Card after required maintenance checks have been completed.
S141: Maintenance authorization is recorded before affected equipment is returned to operational service.
S142: Morrowglass reconciles work across operating areas and preserves a consistent view of task status and outstanding constraints.
S143: Outbound Dispatch Sorter organizes completed pallets according to the current shipping plan.
S144: Outbound Checkweigh Scale verifies shipment weight before the shipping record is finalized.
S145: Shipping Documentation Desk prepares shipment records from confirmed pallet and destination data.
S146: Fire Alarm Panel and Safety Zone Controller provide safety status that can require movement to stop or be restricted.
S147: Warehouse Operations Supervisor reviews delayed tasks, abnormal vehicle stops, and unresolved staging constraints before releasing the next outbound wave.
S148: Exception handling preserves a traceable hold state until the source of a discrepancy is understood and the affected pallet can be safely routed.
S149: A mismatch between expected and observed pallet attributes prevents automatic allocation and directs the load to controlled review.
S150: The operating record retains the scan result, location, and time of detection so that the review can be reconstructed.
S151: Cinderbay consumes its inspection-stage advisory and records whether the pallet can proceed, requires rework, or must remain held.
